judged_text: Office365CalendarService.createEvent still reads only destinationCalendar[0], so the per-host createEvent call for any non-first Office 365 host builds its Graph URL from the first host's calendar externalId. For collective bookings with O365 hosts, the create call for the second and later hosts runs against another user's calendar id and fails; CalendarManager catches the error and the booking is returned as success while those hosts' calendar events are never created — the per-host feature this PR adds silently works only for Google.

For collective bookings with O365 hosts, the create call for the second and later hosts runs against another user's calendar id and fails; CalendarManager catches the error and the booking is returned as success while those hosts' calendar events are never created — the per-host feature this PR adds silently works only for Google.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` to an array and `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now loops over each destination calendar (collective team members) and calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)`. However, `Office365CalendarService.createEvent` still derives its Graph URL from only the first destination calendar (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];` then uses `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId`). It does not select the calendar matching the current per-host credential/destination being processed, so non-first hosts will attempt to create into the first host’s calendar (or fall back to `/me/calendar/events`). This breaks per-host creation for O365 collective bookings compared to the Google implementation, which was updated to select by `credentialId`.
